tier_reason: The lzbench 2.4 README single-thread table has both the 'lzma 26.03' and 'bzip2 1.0.8' rows with exactly the quoted numbers, and states the binary (gcc 15.2.0 release build), options (-eALL -t8,8 -o1c4) and CPU (AMD EPYC 9555P, single thread, turbo off); the benchmark code is public (bench/lz_entropy_codecs.cpp lzbench_lzma_compress/decompress, bench/symmetric_codecs.cpp bzip2) and the flags are in the public Makefile and mk/lzma.mk, consistent with the wave 9 retier-02 treatment of lzbench 2.4 entries.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 15.2.0 (lzbench24_x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc15 release binary), lzbench options -eALL -t8,8 -o1c4; per the public lzbench Makefile and mk/lzma.mk the 7-Zip objects in misc/7-zip (CpuArch, LzFind, LzFindOpt, LzFindMt, LzmaDec, LzmaEnc, Threads, 7zStream, Alloc, Lzma2Dec, Lzma2DecMt, Lzma2Enc, MtCoder, MtDec) are built as C only at -O3 -DNDEBUG -fomit-frame-pointer -fstrict-aliasing -ffast-math -std=gnu99, without 7-Zip's x86 assembler decoder (Asm/x86 LzmaDecOpt, Z7_LZMA_DEC_OPT); bzip2 1.0.8 (mk/bzip2.mk) uses the same flags.
corrections.workload: lzbench 2.4, in-memory, single thread, whole silesia.tar (211,947,520 bytes): compress speed, decompress speed and output size of 'lzma 26.03' (the 7-Zip LZMA SDK code as built in lzbench; the glue in bench/lz_entropy_codecs.cpp actually encodes an LZMA2 stream with Lzma2Enc_Encode2 at the given level and decodes it with Lzma2DecMt_Decode through memcpy-based in-memory ISeqInStream/ISeqOutStream adapters) against bzip2 1.0.8 (BZ2_bzBuffToBuffCompress/Decompress) at several levels.
corrections.stars_or_usage: ip7z/7zip GitHub repo 4.1k stars, 441 forks, 17 commits each a release snapshot by user ip7z (latest '26.04', 2026-10-06), and its GitHub releases carry the official 7-Zip binaries and source archives (7z2604-x64/arm64 installers, 7z2604-linux-x64.tar.xz, 7z2604-src.tar.xz); 7-Zip 26.04 released 2026-10-06 (the 7,243 weekly SourceForge downloads figure is from the search record and was not re-checked); LZMA/LZMA2 are the default methods of the 7z and xz formats
corrections.caveats: Off-baseline win: bzip2 is not one of the spec's general-lossless baselines (zlib, zstd, lz4, brotli, xz), and against the in-list baseline xz 5.8.4 the LZMA SDK row loses on both speeds at about the same size in the same table (xz -9: 2.75 MB/s compress, 122 MB/s decompress, 23.01%, against lzma -9: 2.55 / 78.2 MB/s, 22.97%); zstd 1.5.7 -18 (4.13 / 1175 MB/s, 25.14%) and brotli 1.2.0 -11 (0.56 / 383 MB/s, 23.78%) decode far faster. Against bzip2 -9 compression is about 5.0x slower (derived from page data). The 7-Zip project makes no numeric speed claim for LZMA: DOC/lzma.txt only says LZMA keeps 'high decompression speed and low memory requirements' and compares to nothing; the numbers come from the third-party lzbench README. The lzbench 'lzma' row is not a 7-Zip release binary: lzbench compiles the SDK's portable C code itself (mk/lzma.mk) and leaves out 7-Zip's x86 assembler LZMA decoder (Asm/x86 LzmaDecOpt, enabled by Z7_LZMA_DEC_OPT in C/LzmaDec.c; DOC/readme.txt says 'if you compile the version with Assembler code, you will get faster 7-Zip binary'), so the decode figures likely understate 7-Zip's own builds, and the row is really an LZMA2 stream (Lzma2Enc_Encode2 / Lzma2DecMt_Decode) fed through memcpy-based stream adapters rather than raw LzmaEnc/LzmaDec on buffers. One corpus (silesia.tar), one machine; the lzbench Makefile compiles everything with -ffast-math (irrelevant for integer codecs but non-default). www.7-zip.org does not resolve from this environment (ENOTFOUND), so the SDK page was not read; the ip7z/7zip repo is the official source home in practice (commits by ip7z are the version snapshots and its releases carry the official 7z2604 binaries and source archives) though its README only says '7-Zip on GitHub' and links 7-zip.org. Licence: DOC/readme.txt says the LZMA SDK 'is written and placed in the public domain by Igor Pavlov' and the file headers of C/LzmaDec.c, C/LzmaEnc.c and C/LzFind.c say 'Igor Pavlov : Public domain' (no patent grant); DOC/License.txt puts the rest of 7-Zip under GNU LGPL 2.1 or later, with BSD 3-clause (LzfseDecoder.cpp, C/ZstdDec.c), BSD 2-clause (C/Xxh64.c) and the unRAR licence restriction on the Rar files, so copy only the public-domain LZMA SDK files.

notes: All quoted lzbench 2.4 numbers match the README rows exactly (lzma -9 2.55/78.2 MB/s 48,682,482; bzip2 -9 12.7/35.5 MB/s 54,572,811; lzma -0 29.5/62.3 MB/s 60,520,844; bzip2 -1 13.5/41.1 MB/s 60,484,813) and the derived ratios are correct; tier A kept for consistency with the other lzbench 2.4 entries. Shortcomings to record: off-baseline win (bzip2 not in the general-lossless baseline list), slower than the in-list xz 5.8.4 on both speeds at equal size and far slower to decode than zstd/brotli, compression 5x slower than bzip2 -9, no first-party speed claim, lzbench builds the C-only decoder without 7-Zip's assembler LZMA decoder and wraps it as LZMA2 with memcpy stream adapters, one corpus and machine. Not a duplicate: fast-lzma2 (already verified) is a separate LZMA2 encoder, and xz/liblzma is the separate tukaani implementation and a category baseline.
